notes.detail: Interior is furnished (beds, chests, barrels, furnace, doors) and the towers have corbelled tops, but the outer faces are big flat stone sheets with only a few 1-block slits.
notes.roof: Crenellated fighting tops with a corbel ring are right for a gatehouse, but they are all one grey and the merlon tops are bare.
notes.materials: Stone brick, cobble and mossy cobble work; the two white_terracotta blocks in the dark oak back wall of the gate room clash and read as a face.
notes.levels: L2 banners/bars and L3 slate cones make the three levels tell apart.

visual.summary: Shell of a twin-tower stone gatehouse: open 3-wide passage, gate room above it, stairs up to the wall walk and both crenellated fighting tops, beds and stores inside the towers.
problems: Back wall of the gate room (z 7, x 5..9, y 5..6): the white_terracotta at (6,6,7) and (8,6,7) over the glass panes reads as a face in the back view; use stone brick, spruce planks or a pane/shutter instead.
The passage has no gate at all (x 6..8, z 1..7 open at both ends); a gatehouse should show at least gate leaves or a portcullis groove at L1.

Gate-room front opening (7,5,3) opens onto a 6-block drop into the open recess x 6..8 z 1..2 y 4..6 over the passage; a soldier stepping out falls. Put a railing/bars there in L1 (L2 already adds bars) or floor the recess.
Outer tower faces are flat and bare: add sills/stair hoods under the slits, a string course, or a few lanterns on the fronts.
Reachability: 255 of 258 standing places reached; the 3 unreached are window ledges (4,6,1), (10,6,1) and a corner at (10,5,2). Fine.
